title: The Day of the Cosmic Broom
skyStory: Last quarter, sixty-eight percent, and the moon is lit down one side like a face turning away from the camera. It is still in Aquarius, still tinkering, but now it's taking things apart instead of building them. Most of the month is behind it. Mars wants to keep going. Saturn says every good builder spends time sweeping up the sawdust.

reading: A waning quarter moon is a broom, and today the Tiger is holding it. Look at all the half-started things scattered around you: tabs, notes, projects with names but no second step. Choose three to keep. Thank the rest and let them go.

This will feel almost impossible, because every idea is your favourite child. But the [[Knight of Wands]] reversed has been warning you all month, and it's not mad, just tired. Aim the fire. Archive the rest. Around 4:10, you'll feel lighter, like finally kicking off winter boots in May.
joel.mission: Close every tab or note you haven't touched in a week, and keep only the three that still excite you.
joel.omen: A bin by the curb, full and ready for pickup. Letting go is a chore, but it makes room for something new.

reading: Half moon on the wane, and you're in sorting mode, but a gentler kind than usual. Not a purge, a review. You'll look back over the last few weeks and see a pattern you missed while you were in it, a thread of good decisions running right through the middle.

Name the thread out loud, even just to yourself in the car. It's the [[Six of Swords]] showing you how much water has already passed under the boat. Then drop one small worry overboard, something you've been chewing on since April. Watch it sink. The Mountain keeps the lessons and lets the rest go with the tide.
nancy.mission: Write down three good decisions you made this month, and read them aloud to yourself before bed.
nancy.omen: Driftwood washed up perfectly smooth. Time and water have softened something that used to be rough.
nancy.elementWhy: a small flame for old worries

together.text: The month is turning. Each of you write one thing you're bringing into June and one thing you're leaving in May. Swap lists by text. Then promise to remind each other of the first and never mention the second again.

game.intro: The cosmic broom is out, sweeping the sky tidy. Show us what it missed.
game.prompt: Something with bristles: a brush, a broom, a doormat, a very fluffy cat. Get close enough to count them.
